question: Among established Adélie penguin breeders observed breeding in consecutive seasons, does reproductive failure increase the probability of breeding at a different colony in the following season?
motivation: Palmer colony-level data show a short-lived lag-2/3 association between relative reproductive performance and later redistribution, but colony counts cannot identify individual movement.
The Ross Sea mark-resight archive contains individual breeding histories across Royds, Bird and Crozier and records reproductive outcome.

A direct individual test can therefore distinguish whether one biologically plausible component of the Palmer aggregate signal—performance-conditioned breeding dispersal—exists in an independent Adélie system.

supporting_publication.note: The published 25-year multistate analysis models age, reproductive state and colony movements but does not use previous reproductive success as the focal movement predictor.

required_fields: breeding status sufficient to identify breeders
data_gate.rule: If these fields cannot be reconstructed reproducibly from the public archive and documentation, stop without substituting a weaker proxy.

eligibility.transition_unit: individual-season t to the immediately following season t+1
requirements: individual is classified as breeder in season t
individual is classified as breeder in season t+1
source and destination colonies are observed and belong to the monitored Ross Island set used by the archive
reproductive outcome in t is observed
eligibility.primary_population: established breeders only: individual must have bred in at least one season before t
eligibility.first_breeder_sensitivity: repeat including first observed breeding attempts; this sensitivity cannot replace the primary established-breeder result

exposure.name: failure_t
exposure.definition: 1 if the season-t reproductive attempt produced zero surviving/fledged/creched young under the archive's documented reproductive-outcome coding; 0 if the attempt was successful
exposure.rule: Use the archive's documented binary or count outcome without redefining success after inspecting movement.

response.name: switch_t1
response.definition: 1 if breeding colony at t+1 differs from breeding colony at t; otherwise 0
response.scope: inter-colony breeding dispersal only; within-colony nest/subcolony relocation is not inferred

primary_estimand.effect: common failure-associated increase in next-season colony switching among established breeders
primary_estimand.statistic: Mantel-Haenszel common odds ratio for switch comparing failed versus successful breeders, stratified by source colony and season t

primary_inference.permutation_unit: within source-colony × season-t strata, permute reproductive-failure labels across eligible individuals while preserving the number of failures in every stratum
primary_inference.test_statistic: log Mantel-Haenszel common odds ratio; if sparse zero cells make the odds ratio undefined, use the corresponding Mantel-Haenszel score statistic without changing strata or sidedness
primary_inference.support_rule: observed association in the predicted direction and one-sided p <= 0.05

mandatory_reporting: number and fraction of switching transitions
observed effect estimate and one-sided permutation p-value
terminal_rules: Do not change the response to nonbreeding, disappearance or resighting probability if movement is too rare.
Do not pool nonconsecutive seasons as if they were one-year breeding dispersal.
Do not search alternate failure thresholds, destination definitions, age cutoffs or environmental subsets to rescue a null result.
Do not infer individual public-information use; a supported result establishes performance-conditioned breeding dispersal, not the cue used.
Do not treat a null result as evidence that the Palmer colony-level lag is artifactual; it would reject only this specific individual movement pathway.
Do not link recoded or anonymized IDs to other archives unless the source explicitly provides a crosswalk.
interpretive_bridge_if_supported: A supported individual result would provide an independent mechanism-level analogue for the Palmer aggregate pattern: reproductive performance can influence later breeding-space allocation in Adélie penguins, while the spatial scale and exact lag may differ among systems.
interpretive_bridge_if_not_supported: A null individual result would narrow the Palmer aggregate signal away from inter-colony lose-switch dispersal and toward retention, breeding participation, within-colony redistribution, immigration/emigration beyond monitored colonies or persistent local-state pathways.
